title: Relative projective space
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $r\in\mathbb N$. Let $F=\mathcal O_X^{\oplus(r+1)}$ be the sheaf of free $\mathcal O_X$-modules with ordered basis $e_0,\ldots,e_r$, and let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}(F)$ be its symmetric algebra sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction], with degree-one sections $T_i=j_F(e_i)$. Use the grading by symmetric degree [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]: the degree-$n$ subsheaf is generated by the monomials $T_0^{a_0}\cdots T_r^{a_r}$ with $\sum_i a_i=n$, and degree zero is $\mathcal O_X$. The constructed pair $(\mathcal A,j_F)$ satisfies the symmetric-algebra universal property [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core], so it is canonically isomorphic, preserving $j_F$, to the pair in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. Thus the latter supplies quasi-coherence and the affine-section identification needed for relative Proj; on an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, the standard-basis identification [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] writes this graded algebra as $R[T_0,\ldots,T_r]$ with each $T_i$ of degree one.

Define the scheme over $X$
$$
\mathbf P^r_X=\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A),\qquad \pi:\mathbf P^r_X\longrightarrow X,
$$
using the construction [def-nagata-relative-proj] and its existence and compatible affine restriction isomorphisms [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists]. The standard open $U_i=D_+(T_i)$ is the open specified on each affine base open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ by $D_+(T_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}(R[T_0,\ldots,T_r])$. Its chart identification is the standard affine Proj identification [def-nagata-affine-proj]
$$
U_i\cap\pi^{-1}(V)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\bigl((R[T_0,\ldots,T_r])_{(T_i),0}\bigr),
$$
where degree-zero homogeneous localization has the meaning of [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. These chart identifications are those of the relative Proj construction, including their compatibility with restriction on the base; no separate choice of chart isomorphisms is made.

This is the relative-Proj interface, not the base-change definition of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]; the latter remains the separate interface for downstream results that use only a scheme over the base.

proof.text: The free-basis inclusions and the symmetric-algebra inclusion are module-sheaf morphisms. Their composite sends one to each coordinate generator and is natural under restriction. Ring restriction preserves products and powers, and module restriction preserves scalars. Thus evaluation of each monomial defines a morphism from the structure module, and the coproduct property extends these maps to the finite-free monomial sheaf of each degree.

On an affine open, the projections and inclusions of the finite free structure module identify its sections with a finite coordinate module. Apply the standard symmetric-algebra polynomial equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial], and compose with the actual section map, which is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-affine]. The resulting ring equivalence sends coefficients to the structure map and variables to the specified generators.

Partition the polynomial monomial basis by total degree. Each degree has finitely many exponent vectors, and the finite-free monomial sheaf has these same vectors as a basis of sections. The direct-sum basis, reindexed by all exponent vectors, identifies the affine finite-sum map from homogeneous sections to algebra sections with a linear equivalence. Given morphisms from every homogeneous sheaf to another module sheaf, invert this equivalence on affine opens and sum their images. Restriction compatibility follows on every basis vector and hence on every affine section. The affine opens form a basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], so extend these compatible maps uniquely by the sheaf property. Scalar compatibility is checked on the same affine cover. This proves that the algebra module and its monomial inclusions form a coproduct; no global direct-sum formula for sections on arbitrary opens is used.

The coproduct universal property gives the unique decomposition isomorphism. Its homogeneous inclusions are split monomorphisms. Define homogeneous multiplication bilinearly by adding exponent vectors in the finite-free bases, and take the unit to be the inclusion of the zero exponent vector. Their images in the algebra are ordinary multiplication and the structure map. Injectivity of each homogeneous inclusion then proves naturality, associativity, commutativity and the unit laws, including the equalities transporting the degree indices. The direct affine comparison also supplies quasi-coherence [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-affine]. This constructs the required relative-Proj algebra input.

For uniqueness, the specified algebra and pieces identify the endpoints. Equality of all monomial inclusions determines equality of the decomposition by the coproduct property. Since these inclusions are injective on sections, the multiplication and unit equations determine all the graded multiplication maps and the unit. The remaining fields are propositions, so the full relative-Proj algebra input is equal.

The chosen input satisfies its defining characterization. In particular its algebra is the constructed symmetric algebra, and each generator is the monomial with one exponent equal to one and every other exponent zero. This proves coordinate homogeneity. The affine polynomial equivalence from step 2 is unique by its values on coefficients and variables. The degree-n inclusion has image the span of its degree-n basis monomials, which the same equivalence identifies with the polynomial homogeneous submodule.

Use the existing compatible relative-Proj realization [def-nagata-relative-proj, lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists]. Its local charts are the affine Proj basic-open charts [def-nagata-affine-proj] with the degree-zero homogeneous localization [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. A coordinate restricts to the same coordinate; the Proj restriction morphism therefore pulls its basic open back to the corresponding basic open. For the union over all affine base opens, refine an overlap around each image point by an affine open contained in both members [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Compatibility on this refinement proves that the union restricts to exactly the prescribed local standard open.

blueprint_update.statement:
For $r\in\mathbb N$, define the relative projective-space interface by

$$
\mathbf P^r_X
=\operatorname{Proj}_X
\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X^{r+1})\bigr),
$$

with the symmetric-algebra generators placed in degree one. Its standard
opens are required to be the relative affine schemes of the degree-zero
homogeneous localizations at those generators. The existence and
compatibility of this object are supplied by
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists].
